findings.justification: E7 shows long-term debt as of June 30, 2026 was $31,067 million. E8 shows long-term debt as of June 30, 2025 was $40,152 million. The debt decreased from $40,152 million to $31,067 million, which is a decrease of $9,085 million, not an increase. This directly contradicts the assertion that long-term debt increased year over year.

This passage from the 10-K filing shows the long-term debt balances as of June 30, 2026 ($31,067 million) and June 30, 2025 ($40,152 million). The debt decreased from 2025 to 2026, contradicting the claim of an increase.

This detailed debt table shows the components of long-term debt and confirms the total long-term debt was $31,067 million as of June 30, 2026 compared to $40,152 million as of June 30, 2025, representing a decrease rather than an increase.

The derived metric shows LongTermDebt yoy_growth as -0.226 (approximately -22.6%), indicating a decrease in long-term debt year over year, not an increase. The values show debt went from $40,152 million to $31,067 million.

The XBRL facts show long-term debt decreased from $40,152 million (June 30, 2025) to $31,067 million (June 30, 2026), which represents a decrease of approximately 22.6%, contradicting the assertion of an increase.
